title: Rank-one cotangent sheaves and generic invertibility on smooth integral curves
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $X,Y$ be smooth curves over $k$, meaning separated integral finite-type $k$-schemes of dimension one [def-pc-curve, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and let $h:X\to Y$ be any $k$-morphism. Write $\Omega_{Z/k}$ for the relative Kähler differential sheaf [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] and use module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Every nonempty affine open of $X$ or $Y$ has dimension one, and their structure morphisms are smooth of relative dimension one. Both $h^*\Omega_{Y/k}$ and $\Omega_{X/k}$ are locally free of rank one, that is, Zariski-locally isomorphic to the structure sheaf [def-sc-invertible-module]. For every $\mathcal O_X$-linear morphism $u:h^*\Omega_{Y/k}\to\Omega_{X/k}$, the following are equivalent: $u\ne0$; its stalk $u_\eta$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] at the generic point $\eta$ of $X$ [def-sc-generic-point] is nonzero; there exists a nonempty affine open $V\subseteq X$ on which $u|_V$ is an isomorphism. For every nonempty open $W\subseteq X$ and every $x\in W$, the stalk $(\Omega_{X/k}|_W)_x$ is a nonzero free rank-one $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module.

source.place: Tag 0C1C, lemma-generically-etale, first paragraph of proof; rank-one and generic-point argument; also Morphisms Tag 02G1

proof.text: For $Z=X,Y$, the curve hypotheses give an irreducible finite-type $k$-scheme of dimension $1$. Apply [lem-sc-dimension-locally-algebraic]: every nonempty open $U\subseteq Z$, in particular every nonempty affine open, has dimension $1$, and $\dim_z Z=1$ at every $z\in Z$. The only fibre of $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is $Z$ itself. Consequently its fibre dimension at every point is $1$; together with the assumed smoothness this is smoothness of relative dimension one by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

Apply [lem-sc-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free] with $d=1$ to the two structure morphisms from step 1. It gives $\Omega_{X/k}$ and $\Omega_{Y/k}$ locally free of rank one. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-invertible] to $h$ and $\Omega_{Y/k}$ to obtain $L=h^*\Omega_{Y/k}$ locally free of rank one as well. Put $M=\Omega_{X/k}$. No smoothness, dominance or nonconstancy of $h$ is required for this pullback result.

source.place: Tag 0C1C (lemma-generically-etale), first paragraph; Morphisms Tag 02G1 (lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free); Modules Tag 01C8 (lemma-pullback-locally-free)

proof.text: On any nonempty common trivializing open $T$ for $L,M$, fix generators $e_L,e_M$. There is a unique $a\in\mathcal O_X(T)$ with $u(e_L)=a e_M$. For every open $S\subseteq T$ and $b\in\mathcal O_X(S)$, linearity and restriction compatibility give $u_S(b e_L)=b(a|_S)e_M$. Thus $u|_T$ is multiplication by $a$, and $u_\eta$ is multiplication by $a_\eta$. Such opens cover $X$ by local freeness. If $u_\eta=0$, the injectivity $\mathcal O_X(T)\to\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$ from [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field] gives $a=0$ on every such $T$. The displayed formula and the uniqueness part of the sheaf gluing axiom then give $u=0$. Conversely $u=0$ gives $u_\eta=0$. Hence $u\ne0$ if and only if $u_\eta\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 0C1C (lemma-generically-etale), generic-point assertion in the first paragraph of proof, expanded in local generators; Properties Tag 01ON (lemma-characterize-integral)

proof.text: Assume $u_\eta\ne0$. Take a common trivializing open $T$ containing $\eta$ and its coefficient $a$ from step 3. The field assertion of [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field] makes $a_\eta\ne0$ a unit. By [lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-function], $D_T(a)$ is an open neighbourhood of $\eta$ and $a$ has an inverse there. Multiplication by that inverse, in these same generators, is a two-sided inverse of $u|_{D_T(a)}$. To get an affine open, choose an affine chart $C$ containing $\eta$ (the local affine condition defining a scheme [def-pc-scheme]). Identifying the affine scheme $C$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A$ for $A=\mathcal O_X(C)$, the basic-open basis of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open] supplies $f\in A$ with $\eta\in D_C(f)\subseteq C\cap D_T(a)$. Under this identification $D_C(f)$ is the principal open $C_f$, and clause (0) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-ideals-closed-subscheme] says $V=C_f$ is affine. It is nonempty since it contains $\eta$; restricting the explicit inverse above proves $u|_V$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 01HZ (lemma-f-open), Tag 01I3 (lemma-standard-open-affine), Tag 01IT (lemma-basis-affine-opens); Algebra Tags 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology) and 00E4 (lemma-standard-open); Curves Tag 0C1C local scalar argument

proof.text: Conversely suppose $u|_V$ is an isomorphism on a nonempty affine open $V$. By [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field], the generic point belongs to $V$ and $\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$ is a nonzero field. The restrictions of the two inverse identities to germs show that $u_\eta$ is invertible. In the rank-one trivializations of step 2, a zero map cannot be invertible over a nonzero field, since its composite with any map is zero whereas the identity sends $1$ to $1\ne0$. Thus $u_\eta\ne0$. Together with steps 3 and 4 this proves all three asserted equivalences.

source.place: Tag 0C1C (lemma-generically-etale), first paragraph of proof, reverse implication by taking the generic stalk

proof.text: Finally let $W\subseteq X$ be nonempty open and $x\in W$. A local trivialization of $M$ near $x$ from step 2 restricts to $W$ and then, on germs, identifies $(M|_W)_x$ with $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ as a module over that same ring. Restricting neighbourhoods to $W$ does not change germs since $W$ is a neighbourhood of $x$. Thus this module is free on the element corresponding to $1$. By [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field], $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is a domain, in particular $1\ne0$, so the module is nonzero. This includes $x=\eta$; no closed-point or perfect-field hypothesis is used.

source.place: Tag 02G1 (lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free), rank-one consequence; Properties Tag 01ON (lemma-characterize-integral), nonzero stalk rings

lean.statement: theorem Scheme.Hom.smooth_curve_cotangent_generic_isomorphism {k : Type u} [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (pX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (pY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsIntegralCurve pX] [IsIntegralCurve pY] [Smooth pX] [Smooth pY] (h : X ⟶ Y) (_w : h ≫ pY = pX) : (∀ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U → (U : Set X).Nonempty → topologicalKrullDim (U : Set X) = 1) ∧ (∀ U : Y.Opens, IsAffineOpen U → (U : Set Y).Nonempty → topologicalKrullDim (U : Set Y) = 1) ∧ SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 pX ∧ SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 pY ∧ ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback h).obj pY.relativeDifferentials).IsInvertible ∧ pX.relativeDifferentials.IsInvertible ∧ (∀ (a : (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback h).obj pY.relativeDifferentials ⟶ pX.relativeDifferentials) (η : X), IsGenericPoint η Set.univ → (a ≠ 0 ↔ (PresheafOfModules.moduleStalkFunctor X.ringCatSheaf.obj η).map a.val ≠ 0) ∧ ((PresheafOfModules.moduleStalkFunctor X.ringCatSheaf.obj η).map a.val ≠ 0 ↔ ∃ V : X.Opens, (V : Set X).Nonempty ∧ IsAffineOpen V ∧ IsIso ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).map a))) ∧ (∀ W : X.Opens, (W : Set X).Nonempty → ∀ x : W, Nontrivial ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor W.toScheme.toRingedSpace x).obj (pX.relativeDifferentials.restrict W.ι)) ∧ Nonempty ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (W.ι.stalkMap x).hom).obj ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor W.toScheme.toRingedSpace x).obj (pX.relativeDifferentials.restrict W.ι)) ≅ ModuleCat.of (X.presheaf.stalk (W.ι x)) (X.presheaf.stalk (W.ι x))))
